name: West Ridge Scramble
approach: From the Barclay Lake Trailhead (2,300 ft, ~20-car lot with privy), follow the Barclay Creek Trail a short distance before leaving it to cross Barclay Creek — as of spring 2026 the footlog crossing has been removed for safety with no announced replacement, so expect a rock-hop or ford. Pick up an unmaintained climbers' path up Tailgunner Creek/Tailgunner Ravine; it's brushy with blowdown lower down and passes through a short waterfall ravine before reaching the base of the Tailgunner Couloir. Follow the couloir (steep snow in spring/early summer) to Tailgunner Pass at roughly 5,320-5,400 ft. The round trip is roughly 5-7 miles with 4,500-6,000 ft of elevation gain/loss depending on the exact line and whether Gunn Peak/Wing Peak are combined — budget a long day (8+ hours car-to-car) or plan an overnight camp near the pass.

approach_variants.name: Tailgunner Ravine to Tailgunner Pass
approach_variants.notes: Leave the Barclay Creek Trail within about a quarter mile and cross the creek — do not count on a footlog, and plan on a rock-hop or a ford. An unmaintained climbers' path then follows Tailgunner Creek, brushy with blowdown low down before firming up on more open ground around 3,600 ft. It passes a short waterfall ravine and reaches the couloir, which carries steep snow in spring and early summer. Budget a long day or camp near the pass; combining Gunn Peak or Wing Peak turns this into a much bigger outing.
hazards: Barclay Creek crossing with no reliable footlog
Steep, often corniced snow in the couloir and on the north slope into early summer
Loose rock and exposure on the west-ridge gendarmes
A cliff band on the north side of the pass that blocks a direct descent
Slick rock in the waterfall ravine when wet
approach_variants.baseFinding: The base of the climb is Tailgunner Pass, the broad saddle around 5,320 ft between Gunn Peak's ridge and Tailgunner itself. Finding it starts at the creek: cross Barclay Creek on a logjam roughly two hundred yards upstream of an old spur road, then bushwhack toward an overgrown corrugated culvert, which is the marker for the start of the climbers' path on that bank. At about 4,000 ft the ravine's cliff band forces a class 2-3 scramble around a waterfall, dropping you and re-climbing, and it is slick when wet. Higher, a brushy weakness in the cliff band near 4,400 ft is the way out of the couloir onto grassy slopes and the crest of the west ridge. You know you are at the pass when the ground opens out into a genuinely broad saddle with the upper basin camps on the far side and the couloir behind you. From there the climb is the ridge itself: minor gendarmes on the crest, then a relic cornice headwall below the summit dome and a narrow summit ledge that is the crux and can be icy with snow lingering. Do not cut off the ridge to the north of the pass — a cliff band there stops a direct line.

itinerary.cal: Snow often lingers in the approach gullies and on the ridge into late June/early July, so many parties carry an ice axe (and sometimes microspikes) for early-season ascents; by August the line is mostly dry talus and scrambling.

days.note: From the Barclay Lake trailhead, parties follow the maintained trail briefly before dropping into off-trail travel along Barclay Creek/Tailgunner Ravine, gaining the broad Tailgunner Pass/Gunn Basin area, then scramble the West Ridge to the summit. The whole outing is done car-to-car in a single long day; the crux is route-finding and steep brush/talus on the approach, not the ridge itself, which is class 2-3 scrambling with a short exposed step near the top.
days.title: Car-to-car: approach, West Ridge, summit, return

schedule.label: Leave Barclay Lake trailhead
schedule.detail: Start on the maintained Barclay Lake trail from the ~2,300 ft trailhead.

schedule.label: Leave the trail
schedule.detail: Cut off-trail up the Barclay Creek/Tailgunner Ravine drainage; steep brush and boulder-hopping.

schedule.label: Reach Tailgunner Pass / Gunn Basin
schedule.detail: Broad ~5,300-5,400 ft saddle; views open up onto the West Ridge line.

schedule.label: Start West Ridge scramble
schedule.detail: Class 2-3 terrain, with a short exposed step/headwall below the summit dome.

schedule.label: Summit (5,839 ft)
schedule.detail: Weather on this ridge can turn quickly; most parties don't linger long.

schedule.label: Back at trailhead
schedule.detail: Descend the same West Ridge line back into the basin, then retrace the approach.

days.objective: Summit Tailgunner Peak (5,839 ft) via the West Ridge

itinerary.totalNote: A single long day car-to-car: roughly 8-9 hours, ~3,540 ft gain over ~6.4 miles, most of it off-trail travel to Tailgunner Pass before a class 2-3 scramble up the West Ridge and back down the same line.

descent_text: Reverse the west ridge back over the gendarmes to the base of the summit block, then descend the same line used on the ascent — either downclimbing (or a short rappel through the crux band in early-season snow/cornice conditions) into the Tailgunner Couloir, or dropping the east slope toward the pass/basin if conditions favor it. A cliff band immediately north of Tailgunner Pass prevents a direct descent that way, so don't cut early off the ridge; carry a rope for the occasional short rappel past the corniced step.
beta: From Barclay Lake Trailhead, follow Barclay Creek Trail then leave it to climb the Tailgunner Creek drainage/couloir to Tailgunner Pass (~5,320 ft), a broad saddle between Gunn Peak's ridge and Tailgunner. From the pass, scramble up Tailgunner's west ridge and south-facing scree/rock slopes to the summit dome; a narrow summit ledge is the crux and can be exposed or icy if snow lingers. In late-spring snow conditions parties have instead cramponed up a north-slope snow route and surmounted a corniced west-ridge headwall — a more technical, roped variation not represented by the Class 3 rating.

waypoints.name: Barclay Lake Trailhead (FR-6024)
waypoints.note: End of FR-6024 (Barclay Creek Road); shared trailhead for Barclay Lake, Gunn Peak, Gunn Point, Tailgunner, and Wing Peak approaches via Barclay Creek and Tailgunner Pass.
waypoints.directions: Drive US-2 east from Monroe to Baring. At milepost 41, across from the store, turn left onto 635th Place NE, cross the railroad tracks, go 0.3 mile and keep left at the junction. The road becomes FR 6024 (Barclay Creek Road); follow it 3.9 potholed miles to the road-end trailhead at about 2,300 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required.

waypoints.name: Barclay Creek crossing / leave trail
waypoints.note: About a quarter mile past the trailhead, cross Barclay Creek on a stout logjam ~200 yards upstream of an old spur road, then bushwhack toward an overgrown corrugated culvert marking the start of the Tailgunner climbers' path.
waypoints.directions: Cross Barclay Creek. The footlog is gone, so use a stout logjam about 200 yards upstream of the old spur road, or rock-hop or ford at low water. On the far bank, bushwhack a short way to an overgrown corrugated metal culvert. It marks an old logging road where the Tailgunner climbers' path begins.

waypoints.name: Rocky knob on climbers' path
waypoints.note: Old logging-road tread gives way to a rockier, more open knob roughly 2.8 hours up from the trailhead; route-finding gets easier here as the path steepens into Tailgunner Ravine. The knob sits at ~3,600 ft; position is estimated, not surveyed.
waypoints.directions: Follow the climbers' path up the overgrown logging-road tread and on through forest with fallen limbs and blowdown, steepening to an open rock knob at about 3,600 ft.

waypoints.name: Waterfall ravine
waypoints.note: The 'infamous waterfall ravine' cliff band at ~4,000 ft: a Class 2-3 scramble around a waterfall in the ravine that forces a short descent and re-ascent; slick rock when wet. Position is estimated, not surveyed.
waypoints.directions: Continue up to the base of a huge cliff near 4,000 ft, then angle right about 150 yards to the waterfall ravine. Get past the waterfall with a short class 2-3 scramble down and back up. The rock is slick when wet.

waypoints.name: Brushy cliff-band weakness
waypoints.note: Leave the Tailgunner Couloir here through a brushy weakness in the cliff band to gain the crest of the west ridge; grassy slopes and firm snow patches persist into early summer. Position is estimated, not surveyed.
waypoints.directions: Climb on to about 4,400 ft, where the path forks. The spring line runs straight into Tailgunner Couloir, which holds steep snow early in the season. The summer line curves back to the left and climbs a brushy weakness in the cliff band.

waypoints.name: Tailgunner Pass
waypoints.note: Broad saddle between Gunn Point and Tailgunner reached after ~3,000 ft of gain; couloir approach and the upper Gunn Basin camps converge here. Position is estimated, not surveyed.
waypoints.directions: Above the cliff band, keep climbing to Tailgunner Pass, the broad saddle at about 5,320 ft with Tailgunner rising to the west and Gunn Peak to the north.

waypoints.name: West ridge gendarmes / cornice headwall
waypoints.note: Follow the ridge crest over minor gendarmes; a relic cornice headwall near the summit dome requires careful, exposed scrambling, especially with lingering snow. Position is estimated, not surveyed.

waypoints.name: Tailgunner summit (Peak 5842)
waypoints.directions: Above the headwall, a short, exposed scramble leads to the summit. The narrow summit ledge can be icy while snow lingers.
